markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a small SASRec extension that tests whether recent, repeated interests improve ranking. No improvement is established yet.

**Insights and directions.** Three baseline insights motivate intervention: causal attention supports next-item prediction but does not guarantee current-purpose matching; Electronics’ 14.95% wrong-pair rate identifies a weak ranking tail; embedding similarity near 0.5 provides little justification for collapse regularization. User feedback additionally distinguishes recent specific interests from isolated historical purchases, without providing replacement or compatibility labels.

Three literature insights suggest practical directions: [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) motivates multi-negative objective experiments; [TLSTSRec](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051) motivates separate timescales; [TransGAT](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884336/) motivates distinct relationship channels, although observed transitions cannot establish complementarity.

| Direction | Available evidence | Minimal intervention | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ranking competition | Positive/negative margins | Uniform multi-negative softmax | Unknown false negatives |
| Current-interest selection | Ordered histories | Recent-interest residual | Purpose remains latent |
| Relationship specificity | Titles and transitions | Separate similarity/transition scores | Compatibility remains unverified |

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each cell gives a positive and a limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: Multi-negative softmax [gSASRec motivation] | 3: established; clean comparison | 7: reusable; gains uncertain | 4: discriminates alternatives; no recency mechanism | 9: targets weak separation; training margins are proxies | 2: loss-only; exclusions require care |
| B: Recent-interest residual plus A [TLSTSRec motivation] | 5: compact combination; familiar components | 8: adaptable; sparse histories limit evidence | 8: counters stale and isolated interests; cannot verify purpose | 8: strengthens candidate competition; gate may saturate | 4: small branch; predictor must match |
| C: Similarity/transition residual [TransGAT motivation] | 6: distinct channels; graph fusion exists | 7: relational specificity; noisy edges | 7: more specific support; no compatibility labels | 6: may separate neighbors; graph popularity confounds | 7: sparse graphs; extra inference cost |

**Selected: B.** Add a learned gated residual from the last five nonpadding item embeddings to SASRec’s causal representation. Repeated recent items receive repeated contributions. This explicitly targets stale-history influence and unsupported extrapolation from isolated interests; it cannot identify satisfied durable needs. Train with 32 uniform negatives to address Electronics’ weak separation.

`h=SASRec(prefix); r=mean(E(last5(prefix))); z=LN(h+sigmoid(MLP(h,r))*r); loss=CE([z·E(positive), z·E(negatives)])`.

Exclude known training positives and target collisions. Ablate objective-only, residual-only, and combined changes; select solely by fixed macro validation HR@10. Preserve all four routes, seeds, data path, and predictor serialization. Keep diagnostic interfaces, measure margins through the actual fused scorer, and report unavailable category breakdowns explicitly. Track simulator uncertainty separately from explicit mismatch. All runtime counts against the shared budget.

idea.description: Extend per-dataset SASRec with a gated recent-interest residual and uniform multi-negative sampled softmax. Compare against each component separately before selecting the combined model.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale or isolated historical purchases and broadly related recommendations with insufficient specific support. A recent pooled branch provides a direct source of recent and repeated evidence. Multi-negative competition addresses measured weak positive–negative separation, especially Electronics’ negative 10th-percentile margin. These are hypotheses about mechanisms, not demonstrated validation gains.
idea.implementation_notes: Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, four dataset routes, single-GPU execution, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200. Pool at most five valid prefix items separately at every causal training position; never include future items. Use a shared item embedding and a scalar gate initialized to contribute a small residual. Start with 32 distinct uniform negatives per target, excluding the user's known training interactions and target; reduce the count if the eligible catalog is smaller. Do not apply a popularity logQ correction to this uniform proposal. Chunk valid positions if necessary for memory. Serialize branch parameters and hyperparameters beneath the trial directory and update the predictor writer to reconstruct the identical scorer. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Make view.log2feats return the fused representation and view.predict_score use its actual trained scoring rule. Report measured metrics and definitions, preserve evaluation mode, and mark unsupported metadata diagnostics unavailable. Select using the host's pinned macro validation HR@10; do not access test labels. Use the 20 training-user simulator recommendations only as qualitative evidence, distinguishing uncertainty from explicit mismatch.
idea.pseudocode:
For each dataset and causal training prefix:
  h = SASRec(prefix)
  r = mean(item_emb(last_up_to_5_nonpadding_items(prefix)))
  gate = sigmoid(MLP(concat(h, r)))
  z = LayerNorm(h + gate * r)
  negatives = sample_uniform_unique(eligible_training_catalog, count=32)
  logits = dot(z, item_emb([positive] + negatives))
  loss = cross_entropy(logits, target_index=0)
  update all model parameters
Compare baseline, objective-only, residual-only, and combined models under a bounded shared budget.
Choose by pinned macro validation HR@10.
Export the selected architecture and matching predictor.

originality.positive: Combines an explicit recent-interest residual with stronger candidate competition in a compact, falsifiable intervention.
originality.negative: Both timescale fusion and multi-negative objectives are established techniques; novelty is primarily the task-specific combination.

future_potential.positive: Provides a small foundation for testing when recent evidence should override persistent interests across heterogeneous datasets.
future_potential.negative: Sparse histories may not support reliable gating, and observational interactions cannot establish immediate purpose or compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires only pooling, a small gate, and an objective change while retaining SASRec's embedding and encoder interfaces.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal pooling, negative exclusions, memory control, and matching predictor serialization require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention baseline and item-dot-product scoring architecture.
limitations: Its architecture alone does not establish compatibility, satisfied needs, or immediate user intent.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Studies sampled BCE overconfidence and combines generalized BCE with more negatives.
Motivates an inexpensive objective comparison before replacing the encoder.
limitations: The proposed sampled-softmax intervention is an alternative experiment, not the paper's exact generalized BCE.
Reported results do not establish improvement on this pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: TLSTSRec
contributions: Combines temporal information with long- and short-term sequential modeling.
limitations: Motivates separate timescales but does not validate this particular five-item residual or its benchmark performance.

related_work.title: TransGAT
contributions: Models distinct complement and substitute relationships with behavioral direction.
limitations: Training transitions and textual similarity alone cannot supply verified complement, substitute, or compatibility labels.
